title: Automate standalone binary CI and tagged releases
description:
## Problem

The checked-in `npm run build:standalone` command can produce one embedded CGO-free host executable, but GitHub Actions currently builds only the static Pages artifact. Contributors and users need reproducible Linux, macOS, and Windows binaries plus a clear distinction between continuously updated preview builds and immutable stable releases.

## Approved release policy

Decision `brain-atlas-3mw` selected two channels:

1. Build and test standalone binaries on every pull request and push to `main`; retain short-lived GitHub Actions artifacts with an explicit retention window.
2. After every successful `main` build, update one clearly labeled mutable `nightly` prerelease and its assets. It must never be marked `latest`, must identify the exact source commit/toolchains, and must warn that its tag/assets move.
3. Publish immutable stable GitHub Releases only from deliberate semantic-version tags (`v*`). Never delete or rewrite historical versioned releases.

Do not create a separate GitHub Release for every commit. Clean up superseded assets only within the single rolling `nightly` channel after the replacement is fully built and validated.

## Scope

Add pinned GitHub Actions automation that installs locked Node and Go toolchains, runs the existing Node/Go/audit/publication checks, stages the standalone production site once, cross-builds `CGO_ENABLED=0` executables for supported Linux/macOS/Windows architectures, packages deterministic platform archives, emits SHA-256 checksums and provenance metadata, and uploads short-lived workflow artifacts. Successful `main` builds safely refresh the one mutable `nightly` prerelease. `v*` tags create immutable GitHub Releases with the same verified artifacts only after all gates pass. Keep GitHub Pages deployment behavior intact. Restructure the README around the two primary user paths: open the hosted GitHub Pages viewer or download a standalone Go binary. Move source checkout, Nix/Node/Go setup, local Vite commands, tests, publication builds, and cross-compilation guidance into a clearly separate Development section.

## Security and distribution constraints

Use least-privilege workflow permissions, immutable/pinned action revisions, `persist-credentials: false` in build jobs, no third-party Go modules or native libraries, no secrets in pull-request jobs, and release write permission only in isolated publishing jobs. Preserve the loopback/authentication/cache invariants in `internal/standalone/SPEC.md`. Nightly publication must not expose an unlabeled mixed-commit asset/checksum set during replacement. Release notes and README must disclose that binaries are unsigned unless signing/notarization is separately approved and implemented.

## Non-goals

Do not publish a distinct GitHub Release for every commit; do not delete or mutate historical versioned releases; do not mark nightly as stable/latest; do not add cgo, native WebViews, auto-update behavior, code-signing/notarization credentials, scientific data changes, or runtime network services beyond the existing loopback server.

## Documentation impact

Make the README user-first: lead with the hosted GitHub Pages URL and standalone nightly/stable binary download choices, concise launch behavior, supported platforms, mutable-versus-immutable channel labels, and unsigned-binary limitations. Relocate contributor/source-build material to a distinct Development section without losing prerequisites, verification, publication safeguards, viewing-stability guidance, or standalone build instructions. Also review `docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and publication/release documentation. Record specific no-impact findings for scientific provenance, lesson validation, `DATA_LICENSES.md`, and `CITATION.cff` unless release metadata changes require an update.
acceptance_criteria:
• Pull requests and pushes to main run locked Node install/audit/publication checks plus CGO-free Go tests and cross-build verification. The complete Node suite is a required local Darwin arm64/Nix gate under decision brain-atlas-ek3 and is not partially rerun by the Ubuntu release job.
• Successful builds upload clearly named Linux, macOS, and Windows workflow artifacts with a documented short retention period.
• Every successful main build refreshes exactly one mutable nightly prerelease; nightly is visibly marked prerelease/non-latest and records the exact source commit and toolchain provenance.
• Nightly refresh is failure-safe and idempotent: an incomplete build cannot replace the prior working channel, users never see unlabeled mixed-commit archives/checksums, and cleanup affects only superseded nightly assets.
• A deliberate v* tag creates an immutable stable GitHub Release after all gates pass; retries cannot overwrite a release produced from a different commit, and historical versioned releases/tags are never deleted or moved.
• Release attachments cover the approved OS/architecture matrix, use .tar.gz for Unix and .zip for Windows, and include SHA256SUMS plus commit/toolchain provenance.
• The embedded Vite artifact is production-mode, contains standalone lifecycle code, omits development hooks, and includes the reviewed notices/current public data.
• Workflow permissions are least-privilege; release write access is isolated; actions are pinned; pull requests receive no release credentials.
• Existing GitHub Pages CI/deployment remains passing and ordinary Pages output remains free of standalone lifecycle code.
• The README presents the hosted GitHub Pages viewer and downloadable standalone binary as the two primary user experiences, with working stable/nightly download paths and concise run behavior.
• Source checkout, Nix/Node/Go setup, Vite commands, tests, publication safeguards, viewing stability, standalone source builds, and cross-compilation guidance live in a clearly separate Development section.
• README/security/architecture/release documentation distinguishes mutable nightly from immutable stable downloads, states supported platforms, and discloses the unsigned-binary limitation.
• macOS instructions require checksum verification first, prefer Apple’s one-time Privacy & Security → Open Anyway path, scope any xattr -d com.apple.quarantine fallback to the verified executable, and never advise disabling Gatekeeper, sudo, or recursive quarantine removal.
• Focused workflow tests or dry-run validation, a nightly replacement rehearsal, a tagged-release rehearsal in a non-public/draft-safe mode, and downloaded-artifact smoke checks provide closeout evidence.

title: Two Pi sessions are actively operating on the same brain-atlas-zmq.10 worktree. Which session should own implementation from here?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Two Pi sessions are actively operating on the same brain-atlas-zmq.10 worktree. Which session should own implementation from here?

Context:
This session safely refreshed feature/zmq-10-tract-region-mapping to main and began auditing the pre-existing partial implementation. A separate Pi process (PID 59432, TTY ttys001) is also editing the same worktree. After decision brain-atlas-vat approved the asset-pipeline amendment, that process changed tools/assets/manifest.json while this session was preparing the identical edit and launched uv run tools/map_tract_regions.py --check. Concurrent writes risk overwritten files, invalid RED/GREEN evidence, and misleading verification. This session has stopped file edits; its attempted manifest edit failed before changing anything because the other session had already changed the target text.

Options:
- Let the existing Pi session on ttys001 continue; this session remains read-only and does not edit the worktree (recommended)
- Pause the existing ttys001 session, then let this session take over after confirming no child process or file changes remain
- Create another isolated branch/worktree for this session to perform only an independent review, not implementation

Requested default: Let the existing Pi session on ttys001 continue; this session remains read-only and does not edit the worktree (recommended)
Requesting run: brain-atlas-zmq.10-concurrency-gate
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.10

- Action: Assign one writer for the active tract-region-mapping worktree.
- Scope: Only determines worktree ownership. It does not discard, reset, stash, commit, merge, push, stop, or kill either session and does not change the approved scientific design.
- Consequences: Single-writer ownership prevents lost edits and invalid verification. Letting both sessions continue risks nondeterministic file state and corrupted closeout evidence.
- Reversibility: Ownership can be reassigned later after the current writer reaches a clean checkpoint and all processes are idle.
- Closeout path: Record the owner choice in Beads; the non-owner remains read-only, or takeover occurs only after process/file-stability checks and a hash-preserved handoff.

title: Approve the conservative tract–region endpoint-proximity design for implementation?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the conservative tract–region endpoint-proximity design for implementation?

Context:
The landed anatomy inspector can already project strict relationships without another renderer or transform. I propose: (1) remove the five arrow suffixes from region labels because they imply directed endpoints; (2) add inspectables for all eight association bundles, the superficial-WM layer, and only region shells that pass a reproducible bilateral mapping screen; (3) generate a checked evidence artifact offline from the displayed streamlines and Jülich OBJ shells using pinned Python/trimesh+rtree, exact point-to-triangle surface distance, and no runtime fitting/warp; (4) ignore streamline array order, count either endpoint, and require at least 18/180 sampled streamlines in each hemisphere within both 3 mm and 5 mm screens before projecting a relationship; (5) label every accepted association relationship undirected, dataset-derived, qualified, and low-confidence—never a precise termination, connection strength, population probability, function, or input/output claim; (6) retain threshold-sensitive and rejected hypotheses in the evidence artifact but not as supported inspector links (notably IFOF–OFC is 5-mm-sensitive and SLF II–DLPFC fails); (7) enrich every relationship with method, source links, status, confidence, and direction, while catalog projection automatically exposes undirected records from both tract and region details; (8) add a superficial-WM inspector record with no named region relationship and an explicit no-mapping limitation; and (9) update the reference lesson disclosure, lesson validation, README, architecture/specs, fidelity, scientific traceability, tract provenance, and a new public mapping-method document. The external evidence review verified Yeh 2022 HCP-1065 records and tractography endpoint/assignment caveats; the custom counts remain descriptive project evidence only.

Options:
- Approve conservative endpoint-proximity design
- Use literature-only relationships; do not publish geometric endpoint proximity
- Revise the design before implementation

Requested default: Approve conservative endpoint-proximity design
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.10

Approval preview:
- Action: Implement brain-atlas-zmq.10 on its isolated feature branch after fast-forwarding it to current main.
- Scope: Changes catalog/schema/UI relationship metadata, generated offline mapping evidence, selected inspectables, five misleading labels, fidelity/lesson disclosures, tests, and current documentation. It does not change fibre/region coordinates, geometry, activity, camera, filters, runtime transforms, dependencies shipped to browsers, or the active yum.6 worktree.
- Consequences: The inspector will expose a larger but visibility-filtered set of named structures. Association links will be explicitly low-confidence endpoint-proximity observations, while unsupported or threshold-sensitive hypotheses remain documented but are not projected as supported links. Publication assets gain a small static evidence JSON and method document.
- Reversibility: All work remains isolated on feature/zmq-10-tract-region-mapping until separately approved for merge/push/publication; the branch can be reverted or discarded without changing main or the active yum.6 worktree.
- Closeout path: Record the approved design/plan under .pi/plans, implement with observed RED→GREEN tests, regenerate validators/evidence, run full publication and browser checks plus independent scientific/code review, record evidence in brain-atlas-zmq.10, and close it only if all acceptance criteria pass.

title: Ship standalone localhost Go binary
description:
## Problem
People should be able to run Brain Atlas locally from one platform-specific executable without installing Node or keeping a dist directory beside it. The launcher should open the default browser and retire the localhost server after the last Brain Atlas tab disconnects.

## Scope
Build the reviewed Vite publication artifact in a standalone-only mode, embed it in a pure-Go loopback HTTP server, launch the default browser, and add authenticated same-origin tab-lifecycle tracking with a reload grace period. Preserve the existing GitHub Pages build without lifecycle code. Add focused Go/JavaScript/build tests and update user, architecture, security, and contributor documentation.

## Non-goals
Do not create a native WebView/desktop shell, expose the server to the LAN by default, add cgo or third-party native libraries, alter scientific data or rendering behavior, sign/notarize release artifacts, or tie shutdown to the browser process.
design: Use CGO_ENABLED=0 and only the Go standard library. A conditional Vite standalone mode injects a small lifecycle module; the normal Pages bundle must omit it. The Go server binds loopback, chooses an available port, sets a random HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookie on the root response, and tracks long-held authenticated lifecycle requests. It arms automatic shutdown only after the first valid client, waits through a short last-client grace period, and supports no-open/stay-open overrides. Browser launching uses small GOOS-specific implementations. Unknown static paths return 404 and unsupported methods return 405.
acceptance_criteria:
- A checked-in command builds a platform-specific executable with CGO_ENABLED=0 and all reviewed Vite output embedded; it runs without Node or adjacent assets.
- The executable binds only to loopback by default, prints its URL, and attempts to open the default browser with a no-open override.
- The server exits after the last authenticated Brain Atlas tab disconnects and the grace period elapses; reloads and remaining tabs cancel/prevent shutdown; stay-open disables it.
- The ordinary Pages build contains no standalone lifecycle module or endpoint marker.
- Go and JavaScript tests cover lifecycle tracking, HTTP behavior, and build-mode separation; existing npm tests and the publication build remain passing.
- README, architecture, security review, and contributor verification guidance truthfully document the shipped behavior and limitations.
- Scientific/data provenance has no impact, or any unexpected impact is documented before closeout.

description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve a controlled five-run optic-radiation diagnostic matrix to isolate DSI Studio nondeterminism?

Context:
The exact historical-style replay diverged despite matching the surviving executable, FIB, masks, argv, and observed random_seed=0. Approximate source corresponding to the executable date indicates two plausible sources: bias-field correction reduces per-thread floating sums in scheduler-dependent mutex order, and tracking assigns deterministic per-seed RNG streams to scheduler-selected thread-local trackers. The proposed user-run matrix changes one factor at a time: (1) repeat the exact 6-thread/default-bias command; (2–3) run two 1-thread, explicit-random-seed=0 commands; (4–5) run two 6-thread, explicit-random-seed=0, bias-field-correction-off commands. The agent will only generate hash-checking wrappers; the user will launch them via `!`. Each OR run previously took about 2 seconds and produced under 0.5 MB. No SWM rerun is requested.

- Do not run more DSI diagnostics; keep yum.6 blocked

title: Approve the revised Atlas/Lesson handoff design as the implementation baseline?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the revised Atlas/Lesson handoff design as the implementation baseline?

Context:
The focused source/UX spike confirmed the reset: `Back to atlas`, the brand link, and browser restoration currently call the global-Atlas path, while stage `Explore this scene` already captures the actual rendered lesson camera plus canonical filters. The long Return control dominates because it is the only solid-teal topbar action. This request deliberately supersedes approval `brain-atlas-56i` only for lesson-to-Atlas handoff and session closeout; one renderer/canvas, exact lesson Return, memory-only local import, static history, scientific behavior, and Atlas-as-Home remain unchanged.

Recommended minimal model:
1. Every transition from an active Lesson to Atlas—`Back to atlas`, brand click, stage `Explore this scene`, and browser Back to an Atlas intent—opens one temporary lesson-derived Atlas branch from the actual rendered camera and complete canonical lesson filters. There is no camera/filter snap. `Explore this scene` remains a contextual duplicate entry point for discoverability but uses the same state path.
2. Atlas displays a compact session pair: restrained outlined `Return to lesson` and adjacent quiet `Exit lesson`. The visible Return label omits the long title/scene; its accessible name and title retain `Return to <title>, <position>`. Both keep 44px targets. Return remains more prominent than Exit but neither uses a solid accent fill.
3. `Exit lesson` clears the resume token/session and inspection branches, removes both session controls, replaces the current intent with Atlas, and applies the authored complete default Atlas snapshot with responsive camera fit. Checked lessons exit directly and remain startable from Lessons. A memory-only local lesson gets a focused confirmation: `Exit local lesson? This lesson and your place are not saved.` Actions: `Keep lesson` / `Exit lesson`.
4. Return remains exact. Browser Forward to the retained lesson works until Exit. After Exit, stale local history normalizes to Atlas with the existing not-retained announcement; a checked lesson URL may be deliberately opened again as a fresh lesson. Focus moves to Return on lesson-derived Atlas entry, back to `Back to atlas` on Return, and to the Atlas heading/stage after Exit. Reduced motion changes only transition settlement; no-WebGL provides the same Return/Exit semantics without renderer controls.
5. Compact layout keeps the two short labels, app status yields space first, and no title is truncated into the action. The dark editorial/precision style stays borders-first with teal reserved for focus/hover, not a persistent filled banner.

Options:
- Approve recommended design
- Revise before implementation
- Keep prior persistent-global Back behavior

Requested default: Approve recommended design
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.28

Approval preview:
- Action: Approve a test-first implementation that makes lesson-to-Atlas navigation inherit current lesson state, quiets Return, and adds explicit Exit lesson/reset behavior.
- Scope: Changes Atlas/Lesson navigation/session UI, history/focus handling, and responsive tests/docs. Does not change renderer ownership, lesson parser/content, scientific data/models, persistence, backend, publication, push, or deployment.
- Consequences: The previous distinction between `Back to atlas` (persistent global) and `Explore this scene` (lesson-derived) ends while a lesson is resumable. Explicit Exit becomes the only action that discards the resumable lesson and resets default Atlas. Local unsaved source receives confirmation.
- Reversibility: The behavior is a local code/UI change on a feature branch and can be amended before integration. It supersedes only the relevant part of `brain-atlas-56i`; no remote state changes.
- Closeout path: Record the decision, write/review a small implementation plan, implement under TDD on `fix/lesson-atlas-handoff`, verify wide/compact Firefox/Chromium plus fallback/history/loss-prevention paths, update current docs/specs, close in a signed commit, and request separate local integration approval.
notes: Beads-backed approval resolved as approved: Approved in Pi UI
close_reason: Beads-backed approval resolved as approved: Approved in Pi UI

title: Approve the atlas-as-Home design baseline for detailed planning and implementation?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the atlas-as-Home design baseline for detailed planning and implementation?

Context:
The proposed MVP has no separate marketing Home. The default workspace is the full atlas with existing complete controls and one canvas. A responsive Lessons drawer exposes the checked Draft retina-to-V1 lesson and existing local Markdown import, and later accepts static library records. Atlas and Lesson are symmetric resumable contexts: opening a lesson preserves the prior atlas camera/filter/control state; Back to atlas restores it and exposes a persistent Return to lesson control with title and scene; Return restores source, active scene, page-scroll position, selected visual, rendered camera, canonical filters/playback request, and focus. Transient particles are not serialized, and in-flight camera motion resolves at the current rendered pose. Explore this scene remains a temporary atlas context seeded from the lesson, distinct from returning to the persistent global-atlas workspace. Static-safe History API/query navigation supports Atlas and checked lessons; local lesson source remains memory-only and reload falls back to Atlas with an accessible notice. WebGL failure disables only spatial exploration while preserving the atlas orientation/source surface, lesson drawer, import, lesson prose/images, and disclosures. The implementation must refactor the existing modal Explore shell into a top-level Atlas workspace without creating another renderer/context, retain the dark editorial scientific-instrument design, and preserve compact, keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, CSP, and static-host behavior.

Options:
- Approve design
- Request revisions
- Reject design

Requested default: Approve design
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.24

- Action: Approve the top-level Atlas/Home, lesson drawer, dual-context restoration, and browser-history design as the implementation baseline.
- Scope: Authorizes detailed planning and subsequent `brain-atlas-zmq.24` implementation after plan review. It does not authorize persistence, a backend, reviewed-library content, inspector behavior, publication, push, PR, deployment, or changes to scientific models/data.
- Consequences: The app will eventually open directly into the full atlas; lessons become drawer-launched, resumable guided workspaces sharing the same stage. Existing scene Explore behavior is integrated into the same atlas surface rather than creating a second experience.
- Reversibility: The plan may refine layout details. Changing the top-level mode model, routing, or restoration semantics after implementation would require renewed approval and browser/accessibility migration work.
- Closeout path: Record this decision in Beads, write and independently review a detailed plan under `.pi/plans/`, then implement with TDD and browser evidence on a feature branch; signed local closeout only, with no remote push.

title: Which atlas Home architecture and navigation model should become the MVP baseline?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Which atlas Home architecture and navigation model should become the MVP baseline?

Context:
The current app opens directly in the Draft lesson. `brain-atlas-zmq.24` must make Home the default, keep the atlas first-class, expose the checked lesson and local import, reuse one renderer/canvas, and define Home/Back/Forward semantics that remain static-host safe. No-WebGL Home keeps the semantic atlas overview and lesson/import entry points but disables only 3D Explore.

- Live atlas Home + static-safe query history
- Editorial menu Home; load atlas only after Explore
- Open directly in full Explore with a lesson drawer

title: Approve the detailed shared-Explore design as the baseline for an implementation plan and runtime work?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the detailed shared-Explore design as the baseline for an implementation plan and runtime work?

Context:
The high-level two-entry design (`brain-atlas-zmq.7.1`) and full-control stage entry (`brain-atlas-79w`) are approved. Three approaches were checked. A CSS-only fixed stage is smallest but leaves background/focus semantics weak. A native dialog with the legacy panel still mutating Three.js directly starts with stale controls under lesson visibility/material factors and can snap the camera on filter changes. The recommended design uses one native full-viewport dialog, temporarily reparents the existing stage/viewer controls/Model & sources with placeholders, and keeps one canvas/context. A small renderer-independent Explore snapshot module clones the current effective scene or a versioned complete-atlas default; panel actions update that temporary canonical snapshot through existing allowlisted commands and the same renderer adapter. A narrow renderer bridge captures the actual in-flight camera, synchronizes the existing panel, and supplies keyboard zoom/pan buttons. Return/Escape force-reapplies the immutable authored snapshot and restores exact lesson scroll/focus. This added state synchronization is required by the existing split between legacy panel state and lesson visibility/material factors; it is not a plugin system or second renderer/filter path.

Options:
- Approve recommended native-dialog/canonical-snapshot design
- Revise the design before planning

- Consequences: Both Explore entry points become keyboard/touch accessible and scientifically disclosed without a second canvas. The main implementation cost is synchronizing legacy controls with canonical snapshots rather than allowing direct stale renderer mutations.

title: When a learner explicitly chooses stage-local **Explore this scene**, how should the authored `guided` / `look` / `explore` policy affect controls inside the full-viewport Explore surface?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: When a learner explicitly chooses stage-local **Explore this scene**, how should the authored `guided` / `look` / `explore` policy affect controls inside the full-viewport Explore surface?

Context:
Decision `brain-atlas-zmq.7.1` approves stage-local Explore from the active camera/filters and global Explore from the complete default atlas, with exact authored-state return. The remaining ambiguity is that the current policy means `guided` = no camera manipulation, `look` = orbit only, and `explore` = orbit/zoom/pan plus viewer filters—yet the recorded user need for the deliberate Inspect affordance specifically asks for zoom and pan without gesture conflicts. The checked-in reference has one guided scene and otherwise uses look, so strict policy inheritance would make most stage-local Explore views unable to zoom/pan and none able to change filters.

Options:
- Explicit Explore grants full controls on every scene
- Guided has no local Explore; look/explore grant full controls
- Inherit each policy exactly inside Explore

Requested default: Explicit Explore grants full controls on every scene
Requesting run: brain-atlas-zmq.7-design
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.7

Approval preview:
- Action: Choose the permission semantics for stage-local full-viewport Explore
- Scope: This decides only temporary Explore controls. Normal Lesson mode remains guided/look as authored; global Explore remains full-control; Return always reapplies the authored snapshot.
- Consequences: Full controls on every scene best satisfies the zoom/pan request but treats explicit mode entry as a deliberate permission elevation. Hiding guided preserves its lock. Exact inheritance is strictest but yields limited Explore for current lessons.
- Reversibility: The policy mapping can be changed later in the pure Explore session model and UI, but lesson author expectations and tests would need revision.
- Closeout path: Resolve the Beads decision, write the mapping into the brain-atlas-zmq.7 plan and UI SPEC, then implement with focused policy/return tests.

title: Which motion policy should the expanded early-vision lesson use?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Which motion policy should the expanded early-vision lesson use?

Context:
The renderer can already animate selected named association bundles and superficial white matter. Long tracts use disclosed stochastic 50/50 bidirectional code-like impulses; SWM/U-fibres use zero-mean vibration. The endpoint-region classifier is not yet available, so any SWM shown is broad superficial context—not proof that each fibre connects the highlighted regions. Continuous camera auto-rotation is currently disabled in Lesson mode and would compete with the authored compositions, text reading, and tract motion; Explore mode is the safer place for free rotation.

Options:
- Add selected tracts + SWM to cortical scenes 5–8; keep authored cameras static (recommended)
- Add selected tracts + SWM and design a subtle reduced-motion-safe overview rotation
- Show SWM only until endpoint-region filtering exists

Requested default: Add selected tracts + SWM to cortical scenes 5–8; keep authored cameras static (recommended)
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.25

Approval preview:
- Action: Choose association-tract, U-fibre, and camera-motion policy for the Draft lesson.
- Scope: Would change only authored scene visibility/playback/disclosure (and, only in option 2, add a separately designed camera-motion contract). It would not change tract geometry, direction probabilities, activity engines, coordinate transforms, or Explore mode.
- Consequences: Selected cortical scenes would gain scientifically disclosed motion and richer white-matter context. Broad SWM cannot yet be described as endpoint-specific. Continuous rotation could weaken composition and accessibility, so it is not recommended.
- Reversibility: Fully reversible by restoring scene configuration; no asset or data migration.
- Closeout path: Record the choice on brain-atlas-zmq.25, update lesson disclosures/fidelity references, verify wide/compact/reduced-motion/no-WebGL behavior, and create a separate signed commit before resuming local import.

title: Approve the staged local lesson-import design for implementation?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the staged local lesson-import design for implementation?

Context:
The parser/security contracts and approved UX specification already define strict local validation, immutable all-or-nothing lessons, actionable diagnostics, and DOM supplementary images. The remaining design choice is where import lives before the future atlas Home shell. A focused staged dialog is the smallest reusable surface: it preserves the active lesson until an explicit Open action and can later be launched from Home without changing the parser/controller lifecycle.

Options:
- Approve staged modal import with explicit validation/open and consent-aware HTTPS images (recommended)
- Use a permanently visible side-by-side lesson editor instead
- Implement a separate full-page import mode now, ahead of the Home shell

Requested default: Approve staged modal import with explicit validation/open and consent-aware HTTPS images (recommended)
Requesting run: brain-atlas-zmq.6-design
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.6

Approval preview:
- Action: Implement a header-triggered local paste/file dialog, pure import validation model, in-place lesson activation through the existing runtime, and accessible supplementary-image presentation.
- Scope: Changes the local static app UI, bootstrap/session orchestration, safe visual presentation, tests, CSP image policy, and documentation. It adds no backend, account, persistence, arbitrary HTML, script/style/frame execution, new renderer, coordinate transform, or remote publication.
- Consequences: Opening a validated lesson may contact the explicitly listed HTTPS image hosts; the UI discloses those hosts before activation and uses no-referrer. Invalid input and validation never alter the active lesson or renderer. The later Home shell can reuse this dialog instead of replacing it.
- Reversibility: The feature is local and can be reverted as one Bead/commit. Reloading restores the checked-in reference lesson because imported source is not persisted.
- Closeout path: Record approval in Beads, create an implementation plan, implement test-first, verify valid/invalid/malicious/file/image/no-WebGL/responsive paths, independently review, commit locally, close `.6`, and continue to `.7` without pushing.

title: By “scrolling spine decoupled from the 3D model,” which boundary do you want?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: By “scrolling spine decoupled from the 3D model,” which boundary do you want?

Context:
The approved prototype pins the stage so only prose appears to move, but keeps both under one explicit scroll ancestor. That lets a one-finger gesture beginning on the canvas natively scroll the lesson. A strictly separate prose scroller makes the model a DOM sibling, so canvas gestures cannot scroll it without custom gesture forwarding and non-native momentum.

Options:
- Pin the 3D stage; scroll only the visible prose, but retain one shared scroll ancestor for native canvas swipes (recommended)
- Put the 3D stage completely outside the prose scroller and implement custom canvas-to-prose touch forwarding
- Put the 3D stage completely outside the prose scroller; canvas swipes no longer scroll the lesson

Requested default: Pin the 3D stage; scroll only the visible prose, but retain one shared scroll ancestor for native canvas swipes (recommended)
Requesting run: brain-atlas-zmq.23-stage-scroll-boundary
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.23

Approval preview:
- Action: Clarify whether decoupling is visual/layout-only or a strict DOM scroll-container boundary.
- Scope: Determines stage placement and touch routing. It does not change anatomy, scene content, renderer state, or scrollbar styling.
- Consequences: Shared ancestry preserves native touch momentum while the stage stays visibly pinned. Strict separation requires custom touch forwarding or removes canvas-origin scrolling.
- Reversibility: Either layout can be refactored later, but strict separation adds gesture code and broader accessibility/browser verification.
- Closeout path: Record the choice on brain-atlas-zmq.23, amend the approved plan if needed, then continue the paused TDD integration.

title: Approve replacing root-page scrolling with one accessible below-header lesson scroll surface?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve replacing root-page scrolling with one accessible below-header lesson scroll surface?

Context:
The header is already fixed; absolute positioning would scroll it away. Headed Firefox cannot reproduce DOM overflow but the user sees one-character root-surface displacement. An untracked prototype eliminated root movement and horizontal travel by keeping the browser root fixed and scrolling one explicit surface. This is more reliable than compositor or permanent-scrollbar patches.

Options:
- Approve explicit lesson scroll surface (recommended)
- Use only a permanent root scrollbar/gutter patch
- Defer and gather a Firefox screen recording before changing layout
- Reject this direction

Requested default: Approve explicit lesson scroll surface (recommended)
Requesting run: brain-atlas-zmq.23-scroll-surface-design
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.23

Approval preview:
- Action: Add one named, focusable below-header scroll container around the lesson layout, viewer controls, and footer; lock root scrolling; keep the native vertical scrollbar; pre-stabilize the sticky stage; route scroll navigation, explicit focus scrolling, and compact-modal scroll lock through the new surface.
- Scope: Changes index.html, src/style.css, src/bootstrap.js, focused UI tests, browser regression checks, and synchronized UI/architecture/user documentation. It does not hide/replace the native vertical scrollbar, change scene content or renderer state, implement the atlas home, alter WebGL anatomy/activity, or push remotely.
- Consequences: Firefox no longer scrolls or elastically pans the browser root; below-header content owns vertical scrolling. The scroll region becomes a named keyboard tab stop. Skip links, PageUp/PageDown/Home/End behavior, touch pan-y, scene hysteresis, explicit navigation, focus restoration, compact disclosure locking, and no-WebGL paths must pass regression checks.
- Reversibility: The wrapper and scroll-surface adapter can be removed in one focused revert; lesson data and renderer contracts are unchanged.
- Closeout path: Land only after Firefox and Chromium wide/compact/200%-equivalent checks prove zero root movement/horizontal travel, keyboard/touch and modal behavior pass, 97+ Node tests/build/audits pass, independent review passes, and a signed local-only commit closes brain-atlas-zmq.23.

title: Use physical-distance semantics for impulse speed

title: Approve the layered “Model & sources” disclosure pattern and the companion Spatial Lessons UX/UI specification as the implementation baseline?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the layered “Model & sources” disclosure pattern and the companion Spatial Lessons UX/UI specification as the implementation baseline?

Context:
Recommended design: use progressive disclosure rather than either a single global methods page (too detached) or badges/popovers on every object (too noisy). Keep one quiet, persistent stage-level “Model & sources” control. Beside it, show separate concise statuses for geometry and activity, such as “Geometry: Data-derived · Activity: Modeled”; never collapse mixed representations into one trust badge. On first use of a representation category in a lesson, permit one short contextual note without repeating warnings in every scene. One activation opens a nonmodal wide-layout panel or focus-managed compact sheet, preserving the active scene. Sections are: What is shown; geometry source/processing; activity/direction model; supported interpretation; assumptions and uncertainty; material known limitations; sources and licenses. Status vocabulary is Data-derived, Derived, Mirrored, Modeled, Schematic, Illustrative, and Display-only, with combinations allowed and plain-language explanations required. Show known limitations only when they could materially change interpretation/confidence or when a higher-fidelity replacement is planned; do not expose internal Bead IDs. The same record remains available for keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, and no-WebGL paths. Closing restores focus to the invoking control. Lesson files reference curated entity/model fidelity records rather than duplicating scientific prose or citations. Missing/unknown records are explicit and invalid references fail validation instead of silently appearing trustworthy.

This design fills the fidelity-disclosure dependency in `.pi/plans/brain-atlas-zmq.15-lesson-ux-ui-spec.md`. That companion spec already defines the editorial scientific-instrument direction, lesson/import/explore journeys, wide and compact layouts, surface states, scene hysteresis/re-entry, pointer/keyboard/touch parity, focus restoration, reduced-motion and no-WebGL behavior, and selective Given/When/Then acceptance scenarios. Approval authorizes contract/planning work, not final pixel values or unrestricted runtime implementation.

Options:
- Approve both as proposed
- Request revisions before implementation
- Pause this design gate

Requested default: Approve both as proposed
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.15

Approval preview:
- Action: Approve the progressive Model & sources design and Spatial Lessons UX/UI spec as the baseline for lesson contracts.
- Scope: Authorizes documenting and closing `brain-atlas-yum.3` and `brain-atlas-zmq.15`, then proceeding to the domain-neutral lesson/entity/scene contract work in `brain-atlas-zmq.4` once its remaining maintenance dependency is complete. It does not approve final visual polish, weaken scientific/coordinate/security invariants, or authorize arbitrary external content.
- Consequences: The contracts will encode separate geometry/activity fidelity records, progressive disclosure behavior, responsive layouts, accessibility/focus rules, reduced-motion/no-WebGL parity, and the approved interaction scenarios. Material changes will require an amendment rather than being invented during implementation.
- Reversibility: The baseline can be amended through a recorded Beads decision before or during implementation; runtime work remains test-gated and separable.
- Closeout path: Record the decision in Beads, create the model-fidelity disclosure plan, mark both design specs approved, close `brain-atlas-yum.3` and `brain-atlas-zmq.15` with the approval evidence, and cite them from `brain-atlas-zmq.4`.

title: When you say all tracts should send code-like impulses, should superficial U-fibres/SWM also switch from vibration to impulses?
description:

Question: When you say all tracts should send code-like impulses, should superficial U-fibres/SWM also switch from vibration to impulses?

- Every tract layer, including superficial U-fibres/SWM, uses impulses

title: Which representation policy should govern association-tract activity?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Which representation policy should govern association-tract activity?

Context:
Individual axons conduct directionally, but each displayed HCP/DSI streamline is an unoriented population-tractography trajectory rather than a measured axon. Random per-streamline polarity could create a plausible stochastic simulation, but it would encode an unsupported realization if presented as the data itself. A future evidence-informed model could sample a cited population-level direction distribution while remaining explicitly labelled as simulated rather than measured.

Options:
- Keep the data view direction-neutral; add stochastic direction only later as an explicitly labelled, evidence-informed simulation
- Keep the data view direction-neutral; also allow an optional clearly labelled 50/50 stochastic simulation without supporting direction data
- Replace the current activity with randomly assigned per-streamline travel now, clearly labelled illustrative
- Show only static orientation with no association-tract activity

Requested default: Keep the data view direction-neutral; add stochastic direction only later as an explicitly labelled, evidence-informed simulation

title: Which single reference lesson should validate the first end-to-end lesson system?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Which single reference lesson should validate the first end-to-end lesson system?

Context:
A generic lesson engine should not be designed in the abstract. One real lesson should force the content schema, scene states, camera transitions, visual-rail behavior, mobile adaptation, and free-exploration escape hatch to work together. Reusing the strongest existing assets minimizes new anatomical-data work while keeping the format domain-neutral.

Options:
- How visual fields cross: retina → chiasm → LGN → optic radiations → V1
- How dorsal and ventral visual streams diverge and connect to higher areas
- An atlas orientation tour of cortical regions and major visual tracts
- A deliberately minimal synthetic lesson used only to test the engine

Requesting run: unknown

- Consequences: The existing visual-field pathway has the best data/render coverage and exposes the real-versus-schematic honesty requirements; broader streams require more descriptions and endpoint mapping first
- Reversibility: Later lessons can cover other systems without changing the core format if stable entity and scene contracts are used
- Closeout path: Record the choice on brain-atlas-zmq.1 and make it the first implementation/verification milestone in the roadmap

title: In free exploration, what should be the primary way to discover anatomical descriptions and connections?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: In free exploration, what should be the primary way to discover anatomical descriptions and connections?

Context:
The current layer tree can show/hide named regions and tracts but the 3D objects are not selectable and the manifests contain little explanatory metadata. The least disruptive extension is direct selection: click/tap visible anatomy, highlight it, and open a compact nonmodal inspector while leaving the scene usable. Hover-only UI excludes touch/keyboard users; a full catalog/search system is useful later but is a separate navigation surface.

Options:
- Click/tap a visible region or tract to open a compact side/bottom inspector; add search later
- Search or browse a catalog first, then focus the chosen object in 3D
- Hover labels for quick facts, with click for details
- Show descriptions only through authored lesson links, not through direct atlas exploration

title: What should a learner be able to do after a successful first lesson?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: What should a learner be able to do after a successful first lesson?

Context:
This determines whether the MVP is primarily a spatial explanation, an assessment tool, or a note-making workflow. Embedded quizzes, editable annotations, and notebook round-tripping are valuable but each introduces a separate interaction and content model. - Identify named structures and relationships by freely inspecting a prepared scene
- Demonstrate retention through embedded questions or prediction checkpoints
- Capture annotations or export a lesson-derived note back to their knowledge system

title: While the brain is the dominant inline visual, how much direct manipulation should it allow?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: While the brain is the dominant inline visual, how much direct manipulation should it allow?

Context:
Page scrolling and WebGL navigation compete most strongly over the wheel/two-finger gesture. The conflict can be avoided without making the visual passive: reserve vertical wheel/touch scrolling for the lesson, allow low-risk orbit by dragging, and move pan/zoom plus unconstrained exploration into the explicit pop-out. Camera changes tied to lesson sections should be short transitions between declared views, not continuous scroll-scrubbing.

Options:
- Inline brain is guided/passive; all manual orbit, pan, and zoom require opening the pop-out
- Inline drag orbits, page wheel/touch scrolls; pop-out enables full orbit, pan, and zoom
- Click activates all inline camera controls; Escape releases them back to page scrolling
- Scroll continuously scrubs authored camera paths, with manual controls layered on top

Requested default: Inline drag orbits, page wheel/touch scrolls; pop-out enables full orbit, pan, and zoom
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.1

Approval preview:
- Action: Choose interaction boundaries between lesson scrolling and 3D navigation
- Scope: Defines gesture ownership, focus behavior, camera-transition rules, and the purpose of the brain pop-out
- Consequences: The balanced option preserves tactile inspection without scroll hijacking; full inline controls need stronger focus/escape affordances; scroll-scrubbed camera paths are substantially harder to author, test, and make accessible
- Reversibility: Controls can expand later; starting with explicit gesture boundaries avoids lesson-format lock-in
- Closeout path: Record the choice on brain-atlas-zmq.1 and incorporate it into the interaction contract and technical requirements
notes: Beads-backed question resolved as answered: The lesson needs full brain-model control overall, but each authored scene declares which controls are available. Exploratory scenes may lock filtering/render emphasis while allowing the learner to look around. Guided animation scenes may lock most or all direct manipulation. Vertical scroll remains the canonical scene navigator: crossing stable activation boundaries with hysteresis enters/resets scenes. Scene animations run on their own clock rather than scrubbing continuously with scroll. Provide insensitive/dead scroll zones around active scenes and explicit segment controls to jump, restart, or skip, so incidental scrolling does not disrupt playback. Exact revisit/reset semantics and whether segment controls should cause literal horizontal movement remain to be refined.

title: How should a learner move through a lesson in the first version?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: How should a learner move through a lesson in the first version?

Context:
The lesson document should use discrete semantic steps regardless of presentation. The remaining choice is the primary reading interaction. Scroll-driven storytelling favors study and natural prose; slides favor predictable pacing and presentations; building both shells immediately adds responsive, accessibility, and authoring complexity. Camera motion should follow step changes rather than every pixel of scroll.

Options:
- Scrollytelling: prose scrolls beside a sticky 3D view; each section activates one scene step
- Slides: one full-screen step at a time with Back/Next and keyboard controls
- Guided side-panel stepper: compact text beside the atlas with Back/Next, while free orbit remains available
- Support both scroll and slide presentation modes from the start

Requested default: Scrollytelling: prose scrolls beside a sticky 3D view; each section activates one scene step
Requesting run: unknown
Target bead: brain-atlas-zmq.1

Approval preview:
- Action: Choose the primary lesson navigation model
- Scope: Sets desktop/mobile layout, focus order, history behavior, and camera-trigger semantics; the underlying lesson format will still use discrete steps
- Consequences: Scrollytelling best supports close reading but needs careful sticky/responsive behavior; slides are simpler and presentation-friendly; dual modes roughly double interaction testing
- Reversibility: A presentation-independent step model allows another shell later
- Closeout path: Record the choice on brain-atlas-zmq.1 and use it in the UX design and MVP work sequence
notes: Beads-backed question resolved as answered: Use scrolling as the lesson backbone. Maintain a thin right-side visual rail ordered with the interactive brain first and supplementary linked images after it. Clicking the small brain should open an interactive pop-out/full-screen view that can be dismissed with Escape. Supplementary images may be referenced by external URLs rather than embedded in lesson text. Exact camera transition and embedded-versus-pop-out interaction semantics remain to be decided.

title: What should the minimum lesson-authoring and delivery loop be?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: What should the minimum lesson-authoring and delivery loop be?

Context:
There are two distinct journeys: an external agent authors a declarative lesson, then a learner consumes it. The simplest architecture depends on whether lessons are ephemeral previews, durable project content, shareable pages, or synchronized directly with Obsidian. All but direct synchronization can remain a static site. This decision concerns the first useful workflow, not every future import method.

Options:
- Paste/import locally, validate, and play immediately; no account, server persistence, or public URL
- Agent writes a lesson file into the repository; Vite builds it as a stable static page
- Hybrid: built-in static lesson files plus a local paste/import preview using the same format
- Direct Obsidian integration or sync should be part of the first version

Requested default: Hybrid: built-in static lesson files plus a local paste/import preview using the same format
Requesting run: unknown

- Action: Select the minimum author-to-learner workflow for interactive lessons
- Scope: Determines lesson storage, routing, validation, and whether a backend or Obsidian-specific integration is required; does not settle scroll versus slides or the exact lesson syntax
- Consequences: A local/static choice keeps deployment simple; direct synchronization introduces integration, permissions, and failure-state work much earlier
- Reversibility: The declarative format can support additional import and publishing adapters later if kept renderer-independent
- Closeout path: Record the answer on brain-atlas-zmq.1 and use it to define the MVP architecture and sequenced child Beads

title: Who should the first version optimize for, and what should they accomplish in one visit?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Who should the first version optimize for, and what should they accomplish in one visit?

Context:
The current viewer mixes two modes: a guided visual explanation of retina→LGN→V1 and an expert layer explorer with hemispheres, cytoarchitectonic regions, tracts, cutaway, opacity, and camera controls. A primary audience is needed because the simplest good UX differs sharply: learners need a guided story and progressive disclosure; domain users need inspection, provenance, comparison, and reproducible views. Secondary audiences can remain supported, but one must win when priorities conflict.

Options:
- Curious learner or student — understand the visual pathway and crossing pattern in 3–5 minutes
- Educator or science communicator — present a reliable guided explanation to others
- Neuroscience learner/researcher — inspect named structures, tracts, hemispheres, and provenance
- Portfolio/public showcase visitor — experience an impressive visualization and grasp its core claim quickly

title: Approve relicensing your original Brain Atlas code and documentation from MIT to AGPL-3.0?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve relicensing your original Brain Atlas code and documentation from MIT to AGPL-3.0?

Context:
Git history shows one author, Steve Hay, so no additional contributor consent appears necessary. title: How should the untracked files currently under public/ be handled before GitHub Pages publication?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: How should the untracked files currently under public/ be handled before GitHub Pages publication?

Context:
Vite copies every file under public/ into dist. The current untracked Draco files and OR_L/OR_tmp GLBs therefore enter a local build, but their provenance/licensing has not been established in tracked notices. The new npm run build:publish guard correctly refuses them. A GitHub Actions build from a clean tracked checkout would not contain them.

Options:
- Leave them untracked; publish only from a clean GitHub checkout/Action
- Move them out of public/ into a non-deployed local workbench directory
- Audit, license, and commit selected assets for publication

Requested default: Leave them untracked; publish only from a clean GitHub checkout/Action
Requesting run: brain-atlas-license-review
Target bead: brain-atlas-2pb

- Action: Choose whether experimental untracked assets remain local, move outside the deployment tree, or become licensed publication assets.
- Scope: Only public/draco/* and public/models/OR_L.glb, OR_L_lite.glb, OR_tmp.glb. Existing tracked datasets and application code are unaffected.
- Consequences: Leaving them requires clean-checkout deployment and keeps local build:publish blocked; moving them permits local publication builds; including them requires verified provenance, licenses, attribution, and production references.
- Reversibility: Leaving or moving is reversible; committing publication assets can be reverted but adds redistribution obligations and repository weight.
- Closeout path: Record the decision in Bead brain-atlas-2pb, then verify the selected publication path and include the result in the final commit/report.

title: Apply ponytail simplification audit refactorings
description:
## Context
A read-only repository-wide ponytail audit identified eight low-risk complexity cuts totaling about 114 lines without removing dependencies. Implement them as one focused refactoring change while preserving scientific, security, release, accessibility, and single-renderer invariants.

## Scope
1. Consolidate the eight identical browser-test `monitor(page)` helpers and twelve duplicated `BASE_URL` constants into one CommonJS browser-test helper (`scripts/browser/`).
2. Replace the five duplicate UI `freezeDeep()` implementations with the existing `deepFreeze` implementation from `src/lesson/scene-state.js`.
3. Delete the unused `createSceneInspectionSnapshot` wrapper, its duplicate unit test/import, and its stale `src/ui/SPEC.md` API row; retain `createSceneExploreSnapshot` as the tested implementation used by bootstrap.
4. Reuse `isCredentialFreeHttps` in lesson parsing and Markdown view-model URL validation while preserving fragment-link and image behavior.
5. Replace both manual SHA-256 file loops with Python 3.13 `hashlib.file_digest()`.
6. Replace `cloneCatalogValue()` with native `structuredClone()`.
7. Delete the `clone()` wrapper in `scene-state.js` and call `structuredClone()` directly.
8. Remove the unused `.explore-placeholder-stage` and `.fidelity-status-activity` CSS selectors.

## Constraints
No behavior changes, new dependencies, renderer/coordinate changes, scientific representation changes, publication workflow changes, or security-boundary changes. Preserve generated validators and checked-in asset provenance. Update current subsystem documentation only where the removed API makes it stale.
design: Prefer deletion and existing/native facilities. Keep this as one mechanical refactoring bead; do not broaden it into splitting `bootstrap.js` or `main.js`, changing the lesson contract, or redesigning browser-test infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria:
- All eight scoped cuts are implemented, or any omitted item has a concrete rationale recorded on this bead.
- Focused unit tests, the full `npm test` suite, and relevant browser tests pass.
- Python asset-pipeline tests covering SHA-256 behavior pass under the repository pinned Python 3.13.1 invocation.
- `src/ui/SPEC.md` no longer advertises the deleted wrapper; other documentation is updated only if behavior or interfaces changed.
- `package.json` and lockfile gain no dependencies.
- Final diff is reviewed for preserved scientific, security, accessibility, release, and single-renderer invariants.
- Verification commands, documentation impact, and material deviations are recorded in the bead before close.
notes:
Implemented all eight scoped ponytail cuts as behavior-preserving mechanical refactors. Added scripts/browser/helpers.cjs and consolidated all 14 BASE_URL copies currently present (audit expected 12; anatomy-inspector and home-library had since added two) plus all eight identical monitor(page) helpers. Reused scene-state deepFreeze in five UI modules; removed createSceneInspectionSnapshot, duplicate workspace test/import, and stale src/ui/SPEC.md key-file/API references while retaining tested bootstrap-used createSceneExploreSnapshot; reused isCredentialFreeHttps with fragment-link and image behavior preserved; changed both standalone sha256_file loops to Python 3.13 hashlib.file_digest; replaced cloneCatalogValue and scene clone wrapper with structuredClone; removed both unused CSS selectors. Net candidate: 27 files, 58 insertions, 180 deletions; package.json/lockfiles unchanged and no dependency added.

TDD/refactor evidence: pre-change structural assertion failed on all pending cuts as expected. Focused baseline passed 64/64; focused green passed 63/63 after deleting the duplicate wrapper test. Pinned Python 3.13.1 SHA-256 checks passed empty/small/multichunk fixtures for both implementations. Final staged candidate: npm test passed 247/247; npm run build:publish passed; Chromium Playwright development matrix passed 83 with 4 intentional production/performance skips; git diff --check and git diff --cached --check passed; unstaged tracked diff empty. Visual proof audited at /Users/hays/.betterwright/artifacts/85b42e1702877c85/pi-evidence-1788717474540-5facc7.png. Independent routed read-only review PASS (runtime:delegated-results/018d5caf-cb80-4327-b910-04c2b18c7f0c/child-0.json).

No user-visible behavior or interface semantics, dataset/assets/provenance, citations/licenses, scientific representation/direction/activity, security/release/publication workflow, accessibility contract, renderer/coordinate transform, persistent state/schema, generated validators, dependencies, README, architecture, lesson validation, traceability, DATA_LICENSES, or notices changed. title: Pause animation when the viewer is inactive
description: Reduce laptop battery/GPU use when animation is no longer being observed or intentionally controlled. Before implementation, discuss and approve what counts as inactive and how automatic pause/resume should be communicated; passive lesson reading must not be mistaken for abandonment without a considered timeout.
design: Approved by brain-atlas-ms1. Distinguish requested playback from automatic power suspension. Suspend model clocks and rendering when the document is hidden or the stage is fully offscreen; preserve explicit Play/Pause intent and resume automatically only when observable and reduced motion is not active. Reject keyboard/pointer/touch/scroll idle timers because passive lesson reading and assistive technology cannot be classified reliably. When visible playback is already settled/paused, use event-driven render invalidation instead of an unconditional draw loop. Expose unobtrusive semantic status through the existing model-status/live-announcement path only while automatically suspended; do not add global chrome. Structural asset repackaging/worker parsing remains separate future work. Add pure policy tests plus browser evidence for hidden/offscreen, renewed visibility, explicit pause, reduced motion, and stopped model/render clocks.
acceptance_criteria: A human-approved design distinguishes explicit user pause from automatic power pause; evaluate document visibility, stage intersection/offscreen state, and a resettable keyboard/pointer/touch/scroll idle timer without relying on the limited Battery Status API; preserve the user's intended play state so returning can resume predictably; show an unobtrusive accessible status/resume affordance when needed; do not auto-resume under reduced motion; avoid false pauses during passive lesson reading or assistive-technology use; browser tests cover hidden tab, offscreen stage, inactivity, renewed interaction, explicit pause, and reduced motion; measure that rendering/model clocks stop while power-paused.
notes:
User requested that the interaction policy be discussed when this task is eventually started, not designed implicitly now.
Implementation closeout evidence 2026-07-23: approved policy implemented without material deviation. Pure viewer-power state derives hidden/offscreen suspension, resume eligibility, and continuous-frame need; it rejects idle-time inputs. The one renderer now measures initial stage visibility, consumes the latest queued intersection, cancels frames and freezes all model clocks while hidden/offscreen, shifts active transition clocks, zeros the first resumed delta, preserves requested playback, and redraws paused/settled views only after controls/state/layout/assets invalidate. Existing model-status/live announcement reports suspension/resume with explicit ownership so other status producers are not cleared. The excluded test fails identically on clean main 0ec3c98 because resetLessonActivity repopulates unfiltered association eligibility after canonical filtering; tracked separately as brain-atlas-4px. PR1 contextual L/R selector drift was corrected test-only in explore-edge. Review: initial Gemma pass; DeepSeek found missing reduced-motion clock coverage (addressed); Codex found initial stage measurement, queued-entry, and status-ownership gaps (all reproduced/fixed); fresh verifier refuted the original findings after fixes and found a real resume ownership edge (RED/GREEN fixed); final Gemma/DeepSeek passes reported zero findings. Docs updated: README, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/PERFORMANCE.md, src/ui/SPEC.md, scripts/browser/README.md. No impact on scientific representation/claims, anatomy, dataset bytes, transforms, activity-model direction/rates, citations, licenses, dependencies, security/trust boundaries, notices, release metadata, or CITATION.cff. title: Migrate deprecated Vite and Three.js APIs
description: Follow up the dependency landing by replacing Vite 8 compatibility-mode function-form manualChunks with Rolldown codeSplitting.groups and migrating deprecated THREE.Clock to THREE.Timer without changing animation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Vendor chunk remains separately cacheable and below its warning threshold; animation timing and reduced-motion behavior remain unchanged; publication build and browser smoke pass without warnings; documentation reflects the resulting configuration.
close_reason:
Migrated deprecated runtime/build APIs without changing the visual models. src/main.js now uses THREE.Timer connected to document visibility through renderer-independent src/activity/frame-time.js. The reader updates once per frame, preserves the former first-frame zero and 50 ms maximum delta, rejects negative/backward deltas, and starts from requestAnimationFrame so mixed performance.now/rAF timestamps cannot produce a negative first step. vite.config.js now uses build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting.groups for the deliberate Three.js vendor group instead of deprecated rollupOptions/manualChunks.

TDD/verification: focused RED tests caught the old config, missing timer seam, and a reproduced negative-delta browser crash; npm test passes 21/21. npm run build:publish passes with exactly one cacheable Three.js chunk at 646,501 bytes (162.73 kB gzip), below the 650,000-byte threshold. Searches find no THREE.Clock, manualChunks, or rollupOptions in the migrated scope; production __view instrumentation is absent. Wide Chromium passes both association directions in all 16 groups, pause/resume, anterior and optic-radiation motion, SWM vibration, controls/disclosure, and no application console errors or Clock warning. Reduced-motion Chromium keeps association/SWM model times at zero, 15,000 SWM dots settled, Play/autorotate disabled, and console clean. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md documents the Timer seam and native Rolldown chunking. Independent Gemma 4 31B review returned PASS.

title: Add lesson export and optional GitHub contribution workflow
description: Provide a low-priority path from a validated local lesson to a durable contribution. Start with downloading/exporting the canonical lesson file plus clear repository contribution instructions. Research a backend-free GitHub handoff such as opening a prefilled repository workflow only if it does not require shipping OAuth secrets, retaining broad tokens, or bypassing review. Direct PR creation with authentication is optional and requires a separate security/UX approval.
acceptance_criteria: A validated pasted lesson can be exported losslessly in canonical format; the contribution path preserves required media credits/citations and repository review; no client secret or persistent broad GitHub token is embedded/stored; any authenticated direct-PR path has separate approved threat/UX design and graceful fallback to download/manual contribution; static hosting remains viable.
